evidence.note: Agent enumerated an intended staged pipeline (lexer/preprocessor/parser→AST/type-aware codegen/driver) and a feature set including sized types, structs/unions/arrays, switch, globals — showing conceptual up-front architecture, though as feature lists rather than deep representation rationale.
Explicitly chose a monolithic single main.rs after churn over writing mechanics; internally kept staged structure but no separate semantic-analysis pass and no IR (codegen directly from AST).

First clean build passed 82.8% of tests, evidence the pipeline and its type/scope/AST/lvalue(gen_addr) representations were coherent and general enough to support a broad feature set — beyond a bare minimum.
Array type nesting was inverted (Arr(Arr(int,2),1) instead of Arr(Arr(int,1),2)); a representation flaw found by debugging, not designed-in correctness.
Scoped struct-tag support added reactively via a new SE::Tag scope entry — scoping for aggregates was not anticipated in the original design.

Struct-return-by-value ABI attempted, broke tests, reverted, re-attempted, and abandoned — the architecture could not cleanly absorb this hard feature, indicating it fell short of a design that lets features slot in with minimal disruption.

reasoning: The agent built a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/preprocessor/parser/codegen and reasonable representations for types (sized ops), scopes, lvalues (gen_addr), and struct layout — clearly meeting anchor 5, and the 82.8% first-build pass rate shows the representation was general enough to carry many features, pushing above 5. However it stops short of anchor 8: there is no separate analysis pass, design rationale is stated as feature lists rather than deep representation reasoning, and several hard features (scoped struct tags, type-conversion rules, and especially the struct-return ABI) were handled by reactive patching or abandoned rather than slotting in by design. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
